learnings.question: Which economist and Nobel laureate wrote in 1971 that an information-rich world creates a scarcity of attention?
learnings.learning: In 1971, economist Herbert Simon wrote that in an information-rich world, the wealth of information creates a scarcity of attention — the resource information itself consumes.
learnings.articleTitle: Everybody wants your attention, but not everything deserves it.

learnings.question: What single guiding question does one personal content-curation system use to automatically filter out videos before they reach the viewer?
options: Will this video go viral on social media?
Does this video have at least 100,000 views?
Would a Muslim, Malaysian software engineer early in his career actually benefit from watching this?
Is this video shorter than 20 minutes?
learnings.learning: A personal content engine can run daily, pulling new videos from trusted channels and asking one filtering question — e.g. 'Would a Muslim, Malaysian software engineer early in his career actually benefit from watching this?' — to decide what survives.
learnings.articleTitle: Everybody wants your attention, but not everything deserves it.

learnings.question: What is the name for the psychological effect where writing something down or saving it digitally gives your brain 'permission' to forget it?
options: The Performance Paradox of Cognitive Offloading
learnings.learning: Psychologists call it the 'Performance Paradox' of Cognitive Offloading: the moment we write something down or store it digitally, our brains treat that as permission to let it go.
learnings.articleTitle: Is Your Brain the Worst Place to Store Ideas? Why I Built a Second One

learnings.question: Which 19th-century researcher demonstrated that people forget roughly 80% of newly learned material within 24 hours unless they actively recall it?
learnings.learning: Back in the 1880s, Hermann Ebbinghaus showed that we forget about 80% of what we learn within 24 hours unless we actively force ourselves to recall it — the basis for spaced repetition.
learnings.articleTitle: Is Your Brain the Worst Place to Store Ideas? Why I Built a Second One

learnings.question: In the Scrum framework, what is the main reason for breaking a project into short, repeating cycles called Sprints?
options: To allow for more flexibility and quicker adjustments
To increase the overall length of the project
To eliminate the need for planning meetings
To reduce the number of people needed on the team
learnings.learning: Scrum breaks a project into smaller, iterative cycles called Sprints specifically to allow for more flexibility and quicker adjustments.

learnings.question: In Scrum, which artifact visually tracks the remaining work in a Sprint and shows whether the team is on schedule?
learnings.learning: The Burndown Chart is the Scrum artifact that visualizes a Sprint's progress, showing remaining work and whether the team is on track.

learnings.question: What is the Arabic term for the Islamic concept of mindfulness or God-consciousness that builds self-restraint and purifies a person's intentions?
learnings.learning: Taqwa is an awareness of Allah's presence that builds self-restraint and purifies intentions, fostered through acts of worship.

learnings.question: According to a well-known verse of the Quran, for what single purpose did Allah say He created jinn and mankind?
learnings.learning: Quran 51:56 states: 'I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me,' framing worship as humanity's foundational purpose.

learnings.question: Per the Quran, how small a deed is guaranteed to still be seen and accounted for, whether good or evil?
learnings.learning: Quran 99:7-8 says whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it — no deed, however small, goes unaccounted for.

learnings.question: What is the main reason PCIe devices use a spectrum of power management states rather than staying fully powered at all times?
options: To increase the device's maximum data transfer speed
To simplify the hardware's physical wiring
To extend the physical length of the PCIe slot
To save energy efficiently while staying responsive when needed
learnings.learning: PCIe power management states let a device manage power based on activity, saving energy during idle periods while still being able to resume full operation when needed.
learnings.articleTitle: Power Management States in the context of PCIe

learnings.question: Which PCIe power state is comparable to a computer being completely shut down — the longest to restart, but with the greatest power savings?
learnings.learning: L2 is the deepest PCIe power state, almost completely powering down the device — it has the highest power savings but also the longest wake-up time.
learnings.articleTitle: Power Management States in the context of PCIe

learnings.question: In Islamic theology, what term describes the actual, unfolding occurrence of events in a person's life — as opposed to Allah's complete, eternally-written plan?
learnings.learning: Qada' refers to the actual occurrence of events as they happen, shaped by a person's actions and decisions, while Qadr is Allah's complete, eternal plan already written.
learnings.articleTitle: The Art of Qada’ and Qadr

learnings.question: Which Quranic verse teaches that Allah does not change the condition of a people until they change what is within themselves?
learnings.learning: Surah Ar-Ra'd (13:11) teaches that Allah does not change the condition of a people until they change what is in themselves, underscoring personal responsibility alongside divine decree.
learnings.articleTitle: The Art of Qada’ and Qadr

learnings.question: Despite the 80/20 Pareto Principle, what percentage of the Quran's total text do its top 20 most frequent words actually account for?
learnings.learning: Analysis of Quranic word frequency found the top 20 most repeated words accumulate to only about 20.83% of the text — far short of the 80% a Pareto (80/20) pattern would predict.
learnings.articleTitle: Top 20 Words to Understand the Quran: A Data Analysis using Python

learnings.question: What term describes the small diacritical marks placed above or below Arabic letters to indicate vowel sounds and pronunciation?
learnings.learning: Tashkeel are small markings above or below Arabic letters that indicate vowel sounds — without them, the same spelling can represent different words.
learnings.articleTitle: Top 20 Words to Understand the Quran: A Data Analysis using Python
